guides.title: Is There Anything Left You Can Trust?
guides.description: This lesson explores reasons Christians consider the Bible trustworthy. It introduces Scripture as a source of guidance in an uncertain world. The study connects confidence in the Bible with understanding its message. Its questions encourage readers to examine that confidence for themselves. The aim is to establish a foundation for the lessons that follow.

guides.title: Did God Create the Devil?
guides.description: This lesson examines the origin of Satan and evil. It asks how rebellion could begin in a world created by a good God. The study traces the devil's fall from heaven and his influence on humanity. It considers what that conflict reveals about freedom and responsibility. Readers are encouraged to understand God's character in the face of suffering.

guides.title: Saved from Certain Death
guides.description: This lesson explains the Christian message of salvation through Jesus. It considers humanity's need for rescue from sin and death. The study connects Christ's sacrifice with forgiveness and a renewed relationship with God. It presents salvation as a gift received through faith. Readers are invited to consider a personal response to that gift.

guides.title: A Colossal City in Space
guides.description: This lesson explores the Bible's description of heaven and the future home of God's people. It considers the promised city and the restoration of life without suffering. The study presents heaven as a real destination rather than an abstract idea. Its questions connect that hope with the promises of Jesus. Readers are encouraged to consider what eternal life with God means.

guides.title: Keys for a Happy Marriage
guides.description: This lesson presents biblical principles for building a strong marriage. It examines commitments and attitudes that help couples maintain love and trust. The study considers how faith affects the treatment of a spouse. Its practical focus is on strengthening a relationship rather than merely identifying problems. Readers are encouraged to apply those principles within their own marriage.

guides.title: Written in Stone!
guides.description: This lesson examines the Ten Commandments and their place in Christian life. It asks why God's law was written on stone and whether it has changed. The study considers the relationship between the commandments and God's character. It also explores the continuing significance of obedience. Readers are encouraged to compare their understanding of the law with Scripture.

guides.title: The Lost Day of History
guides.description: This lesson studies the seventh-day Sabbath as a memorial of creation. It examines the fourth commandment and the biblical identity of the day. The study considers why Sabbath observance matters in the author's understanding of Christian faith. It connects rest and worship with recognizing God as Creator. Readers are invited to examine the biblical basis for this practice.

guides.title: Ultimate Deliverance
guides.description: This lesson explores the promised return of Jesus. It considers how Christ's coming is described and what it means for His followers. The study presents the event as the fulfillment of the Christian hope of deliverance. It also connects that promise with preparation and trust. Readers are encouraged to understand the second coming through the Bible's descriptions.

guides.title: Purity and Power!
guides.description: This lesson explains baptism as a response to Jesus and a symbol of a new life. It examines the biblical practice of immersion. The study considers the connection between faith, commitment, and baptism. It asks what the decision communicates about a person's relationship with God. Readers are invited to understand both its meaning and its purpose.

guides.title: Are the Dead Really Dead?
guides.description: This lesson examines what the Bible teaches about death. It considers whether the dead remain conscious or can communicate with the living. The study connects death with the future promise of resurrection. Its interpretation challenges the idea of a naturally immortal soul. Readers are encouraged to compare familiar beliefs about the afterlife with Scripture.

guides.title: Is the Devil in Charge of Hell?
guides.description: This lesson studies the Bible's teaching about hell and final punishment. It asks when judgment occurs and who is responsible for it. The study examines whether suffering continues forever or ends with the destruction of evil. It connects those questions with God's justice and love. Readers are encouraged to evaluate common images of hell against biblical passages.

guides.title: 1,000 Years of Peace
guides.description: This lesson explores the thousand-year period described in Revelation. It follows the events associated with Christ's return and the two resurrections. The study considers the condition of the earth and Satan's confinement. It also examines the close of the millennium and the final defeat of evil. Readers can trace how these events fit together in the lesson's prophetic framework.

guides.title: God’s Free Health Plan
guides.description: This lesson presents biblical principles for caring for physical health. It considers the relationship between everyday habits and Christian stewardship. The study discusses food and lifestyle choices within that religious framework. Its purpose is to encourage responsible care of the body. Readers are invited to examine how health-related choices express their values and faith.

guides.title: Is Obedience Legalism?
guides.description: This lesson asks how obedience relates to salvation by grace. It distinguishes an attempt to earn acceptance from a loving response to God. The study considers why the commandments matter to Christians who trust in Jesus. It connects faith with a changed life rather than religious performance alone. Readers are encouraged to examine whether obedience and grace truly conflict.

guides.title: Who Is the Antichrist?
guides.description: This lesson examines biblical descriptions of the antichrist. It considers the identifying features presented in prophecy rather than relying on popular guesses. The study compares prophetic symbols with religious and historical developments. It presents the author's interpretation of the power represented by those symbols. Readers are encouraged to test that interpretation against the passages discussed.

guides.title: Angel Messages from Space
guides.description: This lesson explores the three angels' messages in Revelation. It considers their calls concerning worship, judgment, Babylon, and loyalty to God. The study presents these messages as relevant to the final conflict described in prophecy. It connects their warnings with the worldwide proclamation of the gospel. Readers are invited to examine what response those messages call for.

guides.title: God Drew the Plans
guides.description: This lesson introduces the sanctuary of ancient Israel and its symbolism. It examines how its furnishings and services illustrate the plan of salvation. The study connects the priestly ministry with the work of Jesus. It treats the sanctuary as a guide to understanding forgiveness and reconciliation. Readers can explore how its details point beyond the earthly structure.

guides.title: Right on Time! Prophetic Appointments Revealed
guides.description: This lesson examines major time prophecies in Daniel. It studies the relationship between the periods described in chapters eight and nine. The author connects their timing with events in salvation history and Christ's ministry. Its approach explains how prophetic dates are interpreted within the Adventist framework. Readers are encouraged to follow the calculations alongside the biblical passages.

guides.title: The Final Judgment
guides.description: This lesson explores the meaning and purpose of God's final judgment. It examines biblical courtroom imagery and the role of Jesus. The study considers why judgment matters to both justice and salvation. It connects confidence before God with a relationship with Christ. Readers are encouraged to understand judgment through Scripture rather than fear alone.

guides.title: The Mark of the Beast
guides.description: This lesson examines the mark of the beast in Revelation. It considers the connection between the mark, worship, authority, and obedience. The study contrasts loyalty to God with submission to the beast's demands. It presents the author's interpretation of how this conflict develops. Readers are invited to examine the biblical reasoning behind that view.

guides.title: The USA in Bible Prophecy
guides.description: This lesson considers the role of the United States in biblical prophecy. It examines the second beast of Revelation through the author's historical interpretation. The study discusses religious liberty and the use of political power in matters of worship. It connects those issues with the final conflict over loyalty to God. Readers can evaluate the proposed identification against the text's symbolic features.

guides.title: The Other Woman
guides.description: This lesson studies the woman called Babylon in Revelation. It examines her symbols, relationships, and influence over religious life. The author connects the imagery with spiritual confusion and false worship. The study also considers the biblical call for God's people to leave Babylon. Readers are encouraged to distinguish loyalty to Christ from inherited religious allegiance.

guides.title: The Bride of Christ
guides.description: This lesson explores the church through the biblical image of Christ's bride. It considers characteristics associated with God's faithful people. The study uses prophetic descriptions to examine belief, obedience, and witness. It asks how a church can be recognized by Scripture rather than appearance or popularity. Readers are invited to compare those characteristics with their own religious commitments.

guides.title: Does God Inspire Astrologers and Psychics?
guides.description: This lesson examines claims made by astrologers, psychics, and supposed prophetic voices. It asks how a believer can distinguish divine guidance from deception. The study presents biblical tests for evaluating spiritual claims. It also considers why apparently convincing predictions require careful examination. Readers are encouraged to seek guidance grounded in Scripture.

guides.title: In God We Trust?
guides.description: This lesson explores trust in God through financial stewardship. It considers the biblical principles behind tithing, giving, and responsible use of resources. The study connects generosity with recognition of God's ownership. It asks how money choices reveal a person's priorities. Readers are encouraged to approach finances as part of their spiritual life.

guides.title: A Love that Transforms
guides.description: This lesson explores how love for God changes a person's life. It connects Christian commitment with attitudes, habits, and practical choices. The study presents obedience as a response to love rather than a way to purchase salvation. Its focus is the transformation that follows a relationship with Jesus. Readers are invited to consider where that relationship calls for change.

guides.title: No Turning Back
guides.description: This lesson examines the danger of repeatedly refusing God's guidance. It considers the Holy Spirit's work in conviction and repentance. The study asks how persistent resistance can lead to a final rejection of truth. It also encourages readers to respond while they remain willing to listen. Its message emphasizes a personal decision to follow God without continued delay.
